domain_label: Cinematography — Camera Movement & Framing Grammar for AI-Generated 9:16 Reels
purpose: A method for the choices a cinematography specialist reasons about when specifying camera work for AI video generation: the fifteen-move table (static, push-in, pull-out, tracking, orbit, crane, gimbal walk, handheld, whip pan, snap zoom, slow zoom, dolly zoom, rack focus, speed ramp, FPV drone) each with its emotional read and director trigger, the one-main-move-per-shot rule with a mandatory speed modifier, the ECU-to-EWS shot-size ladder, 9:16 vertical framing geometry and its move economy, lens language (focal-length feel, shallow DOF, anamorphic cues), and the technique-to-prompt-phrase mapping — with definitions held as FACT per the grounding file's sourced excerpts and every craft mapping honestly carried as ESTIMATE untested until credit runs.
assumptions: no generated-footage dataset is supplied; all scores are heuristic priors and every technique definition is quoted from the grounding research file's search-excerpt-corroborated sources (StudioBinder, Backstage, Artlist, wolfcrow, premiumbeat, Wikipedia excerpts), not from memory

the grounding file's sourcing caveat applies file-wide: theasc.com, studiobinder.com, en.wikipedia.org, help.runwayml.com, and higgsfield.ai were 403-blocked to direct fetch this session, so FACT tags rest on multi-source search excerpts rather than full-page fetches

exclusions: lighting grammar (three-point, motivated light, negative fill, golden/blue hour, luxury lighting signatures) — a sibling KB in this specialist covers it

glossary.definition: The camera physically moves toward the subject; reads as growing intimacy or realization — slow push-ins subtle and natural, fast ones abrupt and stylized [FACT — StudioBinder camera-movements + wolfcrow excerpts, grounding S23-S25].
The camera circles the subject; reads as importance, power, being appraised from all sides — the hero move for a car, a watch, or a person turning [FACT — Backstage/Artlist excerpts, S24-S25].
A very fast pan that motion-blurs the whole frame; injects speed and kinetic energy and doubles as a transition device because a cut hides inside the blur [FACT — StudioBinder whip-pan, S26].
A very fast focal-length change punching in on a reaction or detail; a sudden attention spike with comedic or impact energy (Tarantino, Edgar Wright) [FACT — filmlifestyle/beverlyboy excerpts, S27].

Dollying one direction while zooming the other, so the subject holds size while the world warps; reads as unease and psychological rupture [ESTIMATE — canonical technique, not directly excerpted in the fetched sources].
The focus plane shifts from subject A to subject B within one shot, redirecting the eye and connecting two things without a cut [FACT — MasterClass/StudioBinder/premiumbeat excerpts, S28-S29].

Progressive acceleration or deceleration of motion (or zoom) within one shot — slow-motion savor snapping into real time; emphasizes a flourish and primes a cut [FACT on zoom ramping — beverlyboy S27; time-remap usage ESTIMATE, standard editorial practice].

The standard size vocabulary EWS/ELS, WS/LS, establishing, MS, MCU, CU, ECU — from environment-dominant scale down to a single detail at maximal intensity [FACT — StudioBinder shot-size guide + B&H/LibreTexts, S36-S37].

At 1080x1920, platform UI overlays claim roughly the bottom 20% (like/comment/share stack), right 10% (action rail) and top 15% (branding); critical content lives in the ~15-75%-of-height core, centered [FACT — vertical-video framing/safe-zone guides, S39-S41].

Telephoto focal lengths make foreground and background appear closer together, narrow the field of view, isolate the subject and shallow the depth of field — the paparazzi/surveillance feel [FACT — Videomaker/Tamron/premiumbeat excerpts, S42-S44].

The 2x-squeeze heritage signature: vertical-oval bokeh, horizontal (often blue/amber) lens-flare streaks, wider horizontal capture; instantly signals expensive movie [FACT — Wikipedia/RED/Moment/StudioBinder anamorphic excerpts, S45-S47].

The slow/medium/fast/rapid qualifier Runway's Gen-3 guidance says to ALWAYS attach to a camera-movement term, because the same move at different speeds carries a different read [FACT — Runway help-center article located, excerpts via filmart.ai/Medium guides, S30, S48].

nodes.definition: Establish the frame the whole KB reasons in: camera movement is an emotional grammar, and a director picks a move for its read, never for novelty. The grounding file's fifteen-move table pairs each move with mechanics, emotional read, and the trigger for picking it: static/locked (composed, confident), push-in (growing intimacy), pull-out (isolation/revelation/closure), tracking/truck (companionship, momentum), orbit/arc (importance, power), crane/jib (grandeur, arrival/departure), gimbal walk (dreamlike glide), raw handheld (urgency, documentary authenticity), whip pan (kinetic energy), snap zoom (attention spike), slow zoom (flat, voyeuristic), dolly zoom (unease), rack focus (redirected attention), speed ramp (fluid emphasis), FPV drone (exhilaration, impossible travel) [FACT for the sourced reads — StudioBinder/Backstage/Artlist/wolfcrow excerpts S23-S27; gimbal-immersive and dolly-zoom reads are ESTIMATE as the grounding file tags them]. The selection question for every shot is: what should the viewer FEEL at this beat, and which single move carries that feeling.

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding AI-generation craft rule: ONE main camera move per shot, always named with an explicit speed modifier. Multi-move prompts degrade coherence in current video models [FACT-1src — Kling prompting guidance excerpt S31, corroborated by Runway structure advice S30]. Runway's Gen-3 guidance structures prompts as [camera movement]: [establishing scene] with industry terms (slow dolly in, truck left, crane up, arc right, static shot) and instructs to ALWAYS attach a speed modifier — slow/medium/fast/rapid — because the same move at different speeds carries a different emotional read [FACT — Runway article located, excerpts S30, S48]. The rule turns each 3-6 s micro-clip into a single legible gesture: pick the move from the fifteen-move table, set its speed to match the beat, and refuse choreography stacking (crane-while-orbiting, push-in-plus-whip) inside one generation.

nodes.definition: Treat the static/locked shot as a first-class move, not an absence of one. No movement reads as composed, confident, observational — the director picks it when the frame itself is strong [FACT — movement guides S23-S25 via the grounding table]. For the luxury vertical it is the default: luxury-film guides stress 'barely there' camera motion with one small living detail per shot (curtain moving, steam, glass sweating) to make a static frame feel real rather than frozen [FACT-1src — Upscale Living quiet-luxury piece + luxury-brand-film guides, S20-S22]. A static shot also costs the video model the least coherence risk of any row in the table, making it the safe baseline when a beat does not clearly demand motion.

nodes.definition: Master the z-axis pair. Push-in (dolly in): the camera physically moves toward the subject; reads as growing intimacy or realization, drawing the viewer into a face or object to land an emotional beat — slow push-ins are subtle and natural, fast ones abrupt and stylized [FACT — StudioBinder camera-movements + wolfcrow, S23-S25]. Pull-out (dolly out): the camera moves away; reads as isolation, revelation, scale reveal, or closure — the director picks it to end a scene or reveal the context around the subject [FACT — S23-S25]. Speed IS the meaning dial on this axis, which is exactly why the speed modifier is mandatory: 'slow dolly in' and 'rapid dolly in' are different emotional sentences. In 9:16 this axis is the workhorse because depth travel is fully visible in a narrow frame while lateral travel is not.

speed changing the read (slow subtle vs fast stylized)

pros.example: 'slow dolly out revealing the terrace and coastline' closing a reel with a scale reveal that a lateral truck could not show in 9:16

cons.claim: Overused push-ins become a tic that telegraphs every beat the same way
cons.example: five consecutive clips each ending on a slow push-in, so the emphasis gesture stops meaning anything

nodes.definition: Use the lateral move deliberately. Tracking/truck: the camera moves sideways with the subject; reads as companionship, momentum, 'walking beside' — the director picks it to follow a walk, and parallel trucking beside a moving car communicates speed [FACT — S23, S25, and the Veo guide's parallel-trucking vocabulary S38]. The lateral axis is the move most punished by 9:16: the narrow frame shows far less horizontal world per second of travel than 16:9 does, so a truck must earn its place — typically a tight follow on a walking persona where the subject, not the passing environment, is the content. When the environment IS the content, the vertical frame usually wants a depth or vertical move instead.

nodes.definition: Reserve the orbit/arc for hero moments. The camera circles the subject; reads as importance, power, being appraised from all sides — movement guides say it 'builds intensity or emphasizes power' [FACT — Backstage/Artlist excerpts, S24-S25]. The director picks it for the hero subject of the reel: a car, a watch, a person turning to camera. Because the move itself declares 'this matters', an orbit on a throwaway subject reads as false emphasis. In 9:16 the orbit survives well: the subject stays centered on the vertical axis while the background wraps, so the move loses little to the narrow frame — one reason it outranks the truck for vertical hero coverage. Prompt form ties the arc to the subject: 'camera arcs right around the car, slow orbit'.

nodes.definition: Deploy the crane/jib (boom up/down) as the statement move for openers and closers. Vertical travel, often combined with a pan or tilt, reads as grandeur, omniscience, arrival or departure — the director picks it to elevate a location reveal, open a scene, or close one [FACT — S23-S25]. In 9:16 the crane gains value beyond its 16:9 role: vertical travel is the one travel direction the tall frame displays in full, so a boom up a hotel facade or down from a chandelier to a table converts every pixel of motion into visible reveal. Prompt form: 'crane up from street level revealing the hotel facade'. Like the orbit, it is an emphasis move — a crane on a beat with nothing to reveal is empty grandeur.

nodes.definition: Choose the motion TEXTURE consciously, because it is a register switch. The two must not blur: a half-stabilized wobble reads as neither dream nor document, just as poor generation. For the luxury vertical, gimbal float owns immersive travel beats and raw handheld is reserved for deliberate paparazzi/celebrity-energy beats.

nodes.definition: Use the two kinetic punctuation marks precisely. Whip pan: a very fast pan that motion-blurs the frame; reads as speed, disorientation, kinetic energy — picked for energy injection and, critically, as a transition device because a cut hides inside the blur [FACT — StudioBinder whip-pan, S26]. Snap/crash zoom: a very fast focal-length change; reads as a sudden attention spike with comedic or impact punch — punching in on a reaction or detail, the Tarantino/Edgar Wright gesture [FACT — filmlifestyle/beverlyboy excerpts, S27]. Both are single moves and legal under the one-move rule, but they are loud: they spike energy for a beat, so they belong at rhythm accents and seams, not on contemplative luxury beats. When a whip pan will serve a seam, its direction and speed become a contract with the adjacent clip — the seam-contract details belong to the stitching KB, but the move spec here must record direction and speed.

nodes.definition: Distinguish the three closing-in tools by what the space does. Slow zoom: a lens magnification change with NO parallax — the frame enlarges but spatial relationships freeze, so it reads flatter and more voyeuristic than a dolly, the surveillance/stylized-70s register [FACT on the definition S27; the voyeuristic read is ESTIMATE — common craft teaching, exactly as the grounding file tags it]. Dolly (push-in): physical travel with parallax — foreground and background shift against each other, so the viewer moves INTO the space (see PUSH_PULL_AXIS). Dolly zoom (vertigo shot): dolly one way while zooming the other; the subject holds size while the world warps around them — unease, psychological rupture [ESTIMATE — canonical technique, not directly excerpted in fetched sources]. Picking between them is picking a relationship to the subject: enter their space (dolly), watch them from outside (zoom), or destabilize their world (dolly zoom, used at most once per reel and almost never in a luxury register).

nodes.definition: Use rack focus to move the viewer's eye without moving the camera. The focus plane shifts from subject A to subject B within one shot; reads as redirected attention and as a connection drawn between two things — the director picks it to guide the eye or stage a reveal without cutting [FACT — MasterClass/StudioBinder/premiumbeat excerpts, S28-S29]. It is a legal 'main move' under the one-move rule even though the camera body is static, because the focus travel is the shot's single gesture. Its optical precondition: a visibly shallow depth of field — with deep focus both planes are already sharp and the rack is invisible, so the prompt must pair the rack with shallow-DOF lens language ('focus racks from the champagne glass in foreground to her smile behind it'). In 9:16 it shines because the A-to-B relationship is staged in DEPTH along the center line, which the narrow frame displays perfectly where a lateral two-subject stage would not fit.

nodes.definition: Use the speed ramp as tempo punctuation inside one shot. Progressive acceleration or deceleration of motion (or zoom) within a single shot — slow-motion savor snapping into real time, or real time easing into slow motion; reads as fluid emphasis [FACT on zoom/speed ramping — beverlyboy excerpt S27; the time-remap editorial usage is ESTIMATE — standard practice, as the grounding file tags it]. The director picks it to emphasize a flourish (hair flip, car pass) and to prime a cut: ramping up so the cut lands on peak motion lets the next clip open fast and decelerate, hiding the seam in energy. Under the one-move rule the ramp is a TEMPO modifier on the shot's single move, not a second move — 'slow motion easing into real-time speed as she turns' modifies the turn, it does not add a camera path. Stacking a ramp on top of a second spatial move is where prompts start degrading.

A fast free-flying first-person path; reads as exhilaration — the director picks it for location porn and continuous fly-throughs [FACT — the Runway guide excerpt lists FPV as a prompt keyword, S30]. It is the highest-energy travel move in the table and the least composed: the camera surrenders to a flight path, so it suits location-hero beats (arriving over a coastline, threading a villa arch) and fights every intimate beat. In 9:16 an FPV path must be planned vertically — a lateral coastline sweep shows slivers, while a descent, a climb, or a threading move along the depth axis keeps the reveal inside the tall frame. As with all moves it takes one path and a speed modifier; 'FPV' plus a described flight line is still one move.

nodes.definition: Speak the standard shot-size ladder fluently, because size is the first framing decision of every shot. EWS/ELS (extreme wide/long): environment dominates, subject tiny — scale, place, loneliness or grandeur. WS/LS (wide/long): full body plus enough surroundings to read the location. Establishing shot: the head-of-scene wide that sets geography. MS (medium): roughly waist up — balances subject and environment, the conversational default. MCU (medium close-up): chest up — intimacy without pressure. CU (close-up): the face fills the frame — registers small emotions. ECU (extreme close-up): a detail only (eyes, watch crown, stitching, lips) — maximal intensity and tactility [FACT — StudioBinder shot-size guide + B&H/LibreTexts corroboration, S36-S37]. Naming the size explicitly in a prompt ('extreme close-up of the watch crown', 'wide establishing shot') is itself sourced prompting practice, and pairing size with move (ECU + slow push-in vs EWS + crane) is where the grammar compounds.

nodes.definition: Frame every 9:16 shot inside the platform geometry. Export 1080x1920. Centered composition beats horizontal rule-of-thirds in vertical: UI flanks both sides and the narrow frame reads best with the subject on the center line [FACT — S39-S41]. Face placement: eyes in the upper third, about 30-35% from the top; headroom about 8-12% of frame height (~150-230 px at 1080x1920) — more than ~15% headroom wastes the frame, under ~5% feels cramped [FACT — S39-S41]. These numbers are constraints on the START and END frames of every generated clip: a move that begins safe can end with the subject's eyes in the branding zone if nobody checked the landing frame.

nodes.definition: Choose focal length as a feeling, not a number. Wide lens (short focal length): exaggerates depth and z-axis movement, spaces feel vaster; up close it distorts and can heighten tension or unease [FACT — premiumbeat/Fiveable/craigscameraco excerpts, S42-S43]. Normal (~human-vision) lens: natural, balanced; lets the audience engage 'without distraction' [FACT — S42-S43]. Telephoto (long focal length): compression — foreground and background appear closer together; narrows the field of view, isolates the subject, intensifies emotion, carries the paparazzi/surveillance feel, and produces shallower depth of field [FACT — Videomaker/Tamron/premiumbeat excerpts, S42-S44]. Focal length also multiplies the move: a wide lens makes a push-in's z-travel feel faster and vaster, telephoto compresses the same travel into intensity. In prompts the feel is often named by proxy ('long telephoto lens, compressed background', '85mm look') rather than by strict millimeters.

nodes.definition: Dress the image with depth of field and anamorphic cues deliberately. shallow depth of field is what makes a rack focus visible: the shallower the DOF, the stronger the A-to-B redirect reads
credit-run results for mapped phrases feed back into which vocabulary items are treated as effective per model

conflict_axes.name: quiet_luxury_composure_vs_kinetic_energy
conflict_axes.description: The classic-luxurious register wants static or barely-there motion with one living detail, while reel rhythm and paparazzi grammar want handheld shake, whips and snap zooms.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: composure is the default register; kinetic moves are rationed to explicit energy beats and seams, never contemplative beats

conflict_axes.name: dolly_parallax_vs_zoom_flatness
conflict_axes.description: Closing in by dolly enters the subject's space with parallax; closing in by zoom watches from outside, flat and voyeuristic — the same beat reads oppositely depending on the tool.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pick by relationship to the subject: intimacy beats take the dolly, surveillance/candid beats take the zoom

conflict_axes.name: horizontal_travel_vs_vertical_frame_economy
conflict_axes.description: Widescreen habit reaches for trucks, pans and lateral FPV sweeps, but the 9:16 frame shows little horizontal world, favoring push/pull, orbit, crane and vertical reveals.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: re-rank every 16:9 instinct for the vertical frame; laterals must prove their followed subject stays centered

conflict_axes.name: single_move_coherence_vs_choreography_ambition
conflict_axes.description: Real cinematography compounds moves (crane-into-push, orbit-with-ramp), but current video models degrade on multi-move prompts, forcing one legible gesture per clip.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: one move plus a speed modifier per generated clip; express compound ambitions as two clips joined at a planned seam

conflict_axes.name: named_presets_vs_free_text_vocabulary
conflict_axes.description: Higgsfield's marketed Camera Controls presets promise platform-tuned motion, but their MCP mapping is unenumerated, while free-text sourced vocabulary is verified craft with unknown per-model fit.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: free text until a preset is verified on the live surface; verified presets then win for the moves they cover

conflict_axes.name: anamorphic_special_vs_uniform_signature
conflict_axes.description: Anamorphic cues instantly signal expensive movie, tempting uniform application, but everywhere-anamorphic devalues into a filter look and its horizontal flares fight the vertical frame.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ration anamorphic to named hero/finale shots so the signature stays special and the flares stay rare

conflict_axes.name: shallow_dof_cinema_vs_deep_focus_documentary
conflict_axes.description: Shallow DOF reads as cinema and luxury product photography while deep focus reads as documentary/news — but the connotation is convention (ESTIMATE), and some beats (location geography) genuinely need depth held in focus.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: shallow DOF on people and products by default; hold deep focus only where geography or multiple planes are the content

conflict_axes.name: centered_vertical_composition_vs_thirds_habit
conflict_axes.description: The rule-of-thirds habit places subjects off-center, but vertical UI flanks both sides and the sourced guidance says centered composition beats horizontal thirds in 9:16.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: center line wins in 9:16; express asymmetry vertically (eyes at 30-35% from top) instead of horizontally

conflict_axes.name: fact_definitions_vs_estimate_mappings
conflict_axes.description: The technique definitions are excerpt-sourced FACT, but every prompt-phrase mapping and vertical craft consequence is ESTIMATE untested until credit runs — and the two grades must not blur in downstream use.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state definitions plainly with sources; tag every mapping and geometry-derived consequence ESTIMATE until L5 evidence upgrades it

edge_cases.description: A prompt stacks two spatial moves ('crane up while orbiting the car') and the generated clip degrades into incoherent motion
edge_cases.trigger: choreography ambition ignores the one-main-move rule
edge_cases.mitigation: split the ambition into two clips joined at a planned seam, each with one move plus a speed modifier

edge_cases.description: A movement phrase ships without a speed modifier and the model picks a tempo that inverts the read (fast push-in where slow intimacy was intended)
edge_cases.trigger: the Runway always-attach-a-speed-modifier mandate is skipped
edge_cases.mitigation: lint every prompt for a slow/medium/fast/rapid qualifier on the movement term before generation

edge_cases.description: A whip pan planned to hide a seam is generated with mismatched direction or speed across the two clips, exposing the cut
edge_cases.trigger: the whip's direction+speed contract is not recorded in both clips' specs
edge_cases.mitigation: record direction and speed in the move spec for both sides of the seam and QC the blur match before stitching

edge_cases.description: A lateral truck reveal loses its content into the right-10% action rail and the frame edges of 9:16
edge_cases.trigger: a 16:9 shot list is ported to vertical without re-ranking moves
edge_cases.mitigation: approve trucks only when the followed subject holds the center line; otherwise substitute a push/pull, orbit or crane

edge_cases.description: A generated clip starts with compliant framing but the move lands the subject's eyes in the top-15% branding zone at the final frame
edge_cases.trigger: only the first frame was checked against the safe zones
edge_cases.mitigation: QC both start and end frames of every move against the zone map before accepting the clip

edge_cases.description: Critical content (watch face, caption-adjacent detail) is placed in the bottom 20% and the like/share stack covers it on-platform
edge_cases.trigger: composition ignores the UI overlay geometry
edge_cases.mitigation: keep hero details inside the 15-75% height core on the center line

edge_cases.description: A true wide establishing shot in 9:16 reads as empty because nothing anchors the vertical axis
edge_cases.trigger: an EWS is specified without a vertical anchor
edge_cases.mitigation: give every vertical wide a strong vertical anchor — tower, palms, staircase, or a standing figure

edge_cases.description: A dolly zoom is dropped into a luxury beat and its unease/world-warping read poisons the aspirational tone — compounded by its read being ESTIMATE, not excerpt-sourced
edge_cases.trigger: the vertigo shot is treated as a generic cool move
edge_cases.mitigation: reserve the dolly zoom for deliberate psychological-rupture beats (rare to never in this vertical) and keep its ESTIMATE tag

edge_cases.description: A shot plan names a Higgsfield Camera Control ('Bullet Time') as an MCP parameter although no such exposure was visible via presets_show
edge_cases.trigger: web-marketing preset names are treated as live API surface
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the named UNKNOWN blocker; plan only against tools and presets the grounding file read off the live MCP until the mapping is enumerated

edge_cases.description: The technique-to-prompt table is quoted downstream as verified per-model fact and a failed generation is blamed on the model instead of the untested mapping
edge_cases.trigger: the ESTIMATE tag on the mapping is dropped in transmission
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the FACT-definitions/ESTIMATE-mapping split in every artifact and treat L5 credit runs as the upgrade path

edge_cases.description: A prompt says 'slow zoom in' intending voyeuristic flatness but the model renders parallax dolly travel, silently flipping the register to intimacy
edge_cases.trigger: a model conflates zoom and dolly vocabulary
edge_cases.mitigation: QC generated closing-in shots for parallax and record per-model conflation evidence to route future prompts

edge_cases.description: A rack focus is prompted on a wide deep-focus frame and the A-to-B redirect is invisible because both planes stay sharp
edge_cases.trigger: the shallow-DOF precondition of the rack is omitted from the prompt
edge_cases.mitigation: pair every rack-focus prompt with shallow-DOF lens language and stage A and B on the depth axis

workflow.action: Fix the emotional intent of each beat against the fifteen-move table
workflow.description: For every 3-6 s clip, name what the viewer should feel and shortlist the table rows whose reads carry it
workflow.gate: every clip has a named feeling and candidate moves drawn from the table, none chosen for novelty

workflow.action: Commit each clip to one main move with a speed modifier
workflow.description: Select exactly one move per clip and attach slow/medium/fast/rapid; split any compound ambition into two clips
workflow.gate: no clip spec contains a second spatial move and every movement term carries a speed modifier

workflow.action: Assign a shot-size rung to every clip
workflow.description: Name one ECU-to-EWS rung per clip matched to the beat's intensity, defaulting verticals toward CU/MCU
workflow.artifact: shot-size column in the shot list
workflow.gate: every clip names exactly one ladder rung with its read consistent with the beat

workflow.action: Frame each clip inside the 9:16 safe zones
workflow.description: Place critical content in the 15-75% height core on the center line, eyes at 30-35% from top with 8-12% headroom
workflow.artifact: framing spec per clip (subject position, eye line, headroom)
workflow.gate: start AND end frames of the planned move keep critical content inside the zones

workflow.action: Re-rank the move choice for the vertical frame
workflow.description: Audit every lateral move against the depth/vertical economy; anchor wides vertically; stage two-shots in depth; decide native 9:16 vs reframe fallback
workflow.artifact: vertical audit of the shot list
workflow.gate: every surviving lateral move has a centered followed subject and the generation path (native vs reframe) is stated with its risk

workflow.action: Choose the focal-length feel per clip
workflow.description: Assign wide/normal/telephoto (or a proxy like '85mm look') per the luxury default: normal-to-short-tele personas, tele candids, wide only for architecture
workflow.artifact: lens column in the shot list
workflow.gate: no wide lens on intimate face shots and no telephoto asked to show vast environment

workflow.description: Apply shallow DOF to people/products, deep focus only where geography is the content, and reserve anamorphic cues for named hero/finale shots
workflow.gate: anamorphic appears only on named hero/finale shots and the DOF connotation stays tagged ESTIMATE

workflow.action: Translate each spec into sourced prompt vocabulary
workflow.description: Write prompts in the documented structures: Runway [camera movement]: [scene], Kling subject-tied movement, Veo vocabulary — quoting only sourced terms
workflow.gate: every camera term in every prompt traces to a documented guide vocabulary or is flagged as extrapolation

workflow.action: Compose final prompts through the mapping table
workflow.description: Replace draft phrasing with the table's tested-form rows (push-in, orbit, crane, whip, rack, ramp, size, lens rows), flagging any new phrase as untested
workflow.artifact: final prompt set with row-trace annotations
workflow.gate: every emitted phrase traces to a table row or carries a new-untested flag, and the set carries the ESTIMATE caveat

workflow.action: Check the Higgsfield surface before generation
workflow.description: Use only tools/presets read off the live MCP; if a themed preset covers the beat (e.g. paparazzi), weigh it against the free-text prompt; never pass unverified Camera Control names
workflow.gate: no unverified preset name appears as a parameter and the UNKNOWN-mapping blocker is carried wherever Camera Controls are mentioned

workflow.action: QC generated clips for move coherence and landing frames
workflow.description: Verify single-move coherence, whip direction/speed contracts on seam clips, parallax vs flatness on closing-in shots, and end-frame safe-zone compliance
workflow.artifact: QC log with per-model evidence notes
workflow.gate: each accepted clip passes coherence, register and landing-frame checks; failures record which vocabulary the model mishandled

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty tag dominates every claim: FACT definitions stated with sources, ESTIMATE mappings flagged, the Higgsfield Camera Controls mapping held UNKNOWN
dominance_rules.rationale: the grounding file's sources were excerpt-only (403-blocked pages) and the prompt mappings are untested craft, so grade inflation would fabricate certainty
dominance_rules.trigger: any technique definition, prompt phrase or platform capability is stated downstream
dominance_rules.action: carry the grounding file's tag with the claim and never upgrade ESTIMATE or UNKNOWN without new evidence

dominance_rules.rule: The one-main-move rule dominates choreography ambition
dominance_rules.rationale: multi-move prompts degrade coherence in current video models per Kling guidance corroborated by Runway
dominance_rules.trigger: a shot spec or prompt contains more than one spatial camera move
dominance_rules.action: cut to one move plus a speed modifier, and split compound ambitions into two clips joined at a planned seam

dominance_rules.rule: The mandatory speed modifier dominates unqualified movement terms
dominance_rules.rationale: Runway guidance says to always attach slow/medium/fast/rapid because speed changes the emotional read of the same move
dominance_rules.trigger: a movement term appears in a prompt without a speed qualifier
dominance_rules.action: add the modifier that matches the beat before the prompt is eligible for generation

dominance_rules.rule: Safe-zone geometry dominates compositional preference in 9:16
dominance_rules.rationale: platform UI provably overlays the bottom ~20%, right ~10% and top ~15%, so content there is lost regardless of beauty
dominance_rules.trigger: a framing places critical content outside the 15-75% centered core on either the start or end frame
dominance_rules.action: reframe to the center-line core with eyes at 30-35% from top before generation

dominance_rules.rule: Vertical move economy dominates 16:9 lateral habit
dominance_rules.rationale: the narrow frame shows little horizontal world, so depth and vertical moves do more work per pixel (geometry-derived ESTIMATE)
dominance_rules.trigger: a shot list ported from widescreen instinct contains trucks, pans or lateral FPV sweeps
dominance_rules.action: re-rank toward push/pull, orbit, crane and vertical reveals; approve laterals only with a centered followed subject

dominance_rules.rule: The quiet-luxury static default dominates energy injection outside designated beats
dominance_rules.rationale: the vertical's register is composed and barely-there per the luxury-film guidance; kinetic texture is a rationed spice
dominance_rules.trigger: handheld shake, whip pans or snap zooms appear on a contemplative beat
dominance_rules.action: restore static/barely-there motion and move the kinetic device to an energy beat or seam

dominance_rules.rationale: each move carries a sourced read, so a move chosen for coolness fights the beat's feeling
dominance_rules.trigger: a move is proposed without a named feeling it serves
dominance_rules.action: name the intended feeling first and select the table row that carries it, or default to static

dominance_rules.rule: Free-text sourced vocabulary dominates unverified platform preset names
dominance_rules.rationale: the Camera Controls to MCP mapping is a named UNKNOWN, while the guide vocabularies are excerpt-sourced
dominance_rules.trigger: a shot plan wants to reference a Higgsfield Camera Control not visible on the live surface
dominance_rules.action: use the mapping table's free-text phrase and record the preset as a revisit item until the surface is enumerated

dominance_rules.rule: Anamorphic rationing dominates uniform signature application
dominance_rules.rationale: everywhere-anamorphic devalues the expensive-movie signal and its horizontal flares fight the 9:16 frame
dominance_rules.trigger: anamorphic cues appear on a non-hero shot
dominance_rules.action: strip the cues back to shallow DOF and reserve anamorphic for the named hero/finale shots

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the beat's feeling and pick the single move before writing any prompt text
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rewriting whole prompt sets after discovering the move fights the beat or violates the one-move rule

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lint every prompt for exactly one spatial move and a speed modifier before spending generation credit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: burning credit runs on multi-move or tempo-ambiguous prompts that degrade predictably

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix shot size and safe-zone placement before generating keyframe stills
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating stills because faces or hero details landed under platform UI or off the center line

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the move's END frame against the safe zones at planning time, not just the start frame
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discarding otherwise-good clips whose landing frame drifted into the branding or caption zones

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose lens and DOF language at prompt time rather than hoping to fix the look in post
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reshooting clips whose deep-focus or distorted-wide look cannot be converted to the luxury register afterward

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record whip-pan direction and speed in both adjacent clip specs before generating either side of a seam
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating seam clips because the blur direction or tempo mismatched across the cut

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm a Higgsfield preset or tool exists on the live MCP surface before building a shot plan around it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-planning an entire reel when a marketed Camera Control turns out not to be an exposed parameter

anti_rework_rules.rule: Generate native 9:16 unless reframe is a deliberate, stated fallback
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-composition rework when a wide generation reframes badly and the vertical framing must be rebuilt

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the ESTIMATE tag on every mapping-table row until an L5 credit run tests it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: downstream teams hard-coding untested phrases as truths and misattributing failures to models

iteration_protocol.trigger: L5 credit runs produce per-model evidence on which prompt phrases execute as intended
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade or downgrade the mapping table rows per model, replacing ESTIMATE tags with tested status

iteration_protocol.trigger: the Higgsfield-surface research file enumerates the Camera Controls to MCP parameter mapping
iteration_protocol.action: resolve the UNKNOWN blocker, add verified presets as first-class routes, and update the preset-vs-free-text resolution rule

iteration_protocol.trigger: a model update claims or shows coherent multi-move handling
iteration_protocol.action: run controlled two-move tests and relax or reaffirm the one-main-move rule per model

iteration_protocol.trigger: the 403-blocked sources (Runway help center, higgsfield.ai pages, studiobinder.com, theasc.com) become fetchable
iteration_protocol.action: verify every excerpt-based definition and vocabulary against the full pages and correct any paraphrase drift

iteration_protocol.trigger: QC finds a model conflating zoom with dolly or ignoring motion-texture words
iteration_protocol.action: record the per-model conflation, route affected registers to different vocabulary or models, and update the closing-in and texture nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a platform UI update changes the vertical overlay geometry
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure the safe zones, update the numeric constraints and re-audit standing shot lists

iteration_protocol.trigger: reframe-tool output quality is measured against native 9:16 generations
iteration_protocol.action: settle the native-vs-reframe preference with evidence and update the fallback guidance

iteration_protocol.trigger: retention or engagement review shows the static-default register underperforming on the platform
iteration_protocol.action: rebalance the composure-vs-energy default and adjust the kinetic rationing rules

priority_rationale: The grammar frame and the one-move-plus-speed rule come first because every downstream choice — which move, at what tempo — is read against the fifteen-move table and the AI-generation constraint; the individual move nodes then instantiate the table's reads; the framing stack (shot-size ladder, safe zones, vertical move economy) and the lens stack (focal feel, DOF/anamorphic) follow because they condition how any chosen move is framed and dressed in 9:16; and the prompting stack (sourced vocabulary, mapping table, Higgsfield surface) comes last because it translates every upstream decision into generation-ready text while carrying the FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN honesty grades forward.
